title.zh: 卷386 列傳一百七十三 文庆 文祥 宝鋆
title.en: Volume 386 Biographies 173: Wen Qing, Wen Xiang, Bao Yun
title.raw: 卷386 列傳一百七十三 文庆 文祥 宝鋆

sentences.zh: 文慶，字孔修，費莫氏，滿州鑲紅旗人，兩廣總督永保之孫也。

translations.literal: Wen Qing, style name Kongxiu, of the Feimo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner, was the grandson of Yongbao, Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing, whose style was Kongxiu, belonged to the Feimo clan and came from the Manchu Bordered Red Banner; he was a grandson of Yongbao, who had served as governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Daoguang reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a Compiler.

sentences.zh: 五遷至詹事。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he rose to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 歷通政使、左副都御史、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He successively served as Commissioner of the Transmission Office, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as commissioner of the Transmission Office, left vice censor-in-chief, and a grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授禮部侍郎，兼副都統。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently serving as Vice Banner Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the reign he was made vice minister of rites and concurrently vice banner commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，總理孝慎皇后喪儀，會奏軍民薙發及停止宴會期限疏中，誤引「百姓如喪考妣，四海遏密八音」語，下諸臣嚴議。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he oversaw the mourning rites for Empress Xiaoshen. In a joint memorial on the periods for tonsure by military and civilians and for suspension of banquets, he mistakenly quoted the phrase "the common people mourned as for father and mother; throughout the four seas music was hushed for eight tones." The matter was referred to the ministers for strict deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he directed the mourning ceremonies for Empress Xiaoshen. In a joint memorial setting out the periods for military and civilian tonsure and for suspending banquets, he wrongly cited the lines “The people mourned as for a father and mother, and music was stilled throughout the realm”—language appropriate to an emperor's death, not an empress's. The case was sent to the ministers for severe review.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以文慶翰林出身，隨聲附和，獨重譴，褫副都統，降三品頂戴。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor, considering that Wen Qing was of Hanlin origin and had echoed others' views, imposed a punishment on him alone that was especially severe: he was stripped of his post as Vice Banner Commander and demoted to a third-rank peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daoguang held that Wen Qing, as a Hanlin graduate, had merely echoed others; Wen Qing alone received a heavy penalty—loss of his vice banner command and demotion to third-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋復之，歷吏部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was restored; he successively served as Vice Minister of the Board of Personnel and Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored and served in turn as vice minister of personnel and of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十六年，偕尚書湯金釗赴陝西、四川按劾巡撫楊名颺、布政使李羲文，並下嚴議，尋复按名颺被訐事，褫其職。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, together with Minister Tang Jinzhao he went to Shaanxi and Sichuan to investigate and impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Yiwen; both were referred to strict deliberation. Soon after, upon reinvestigating the matter of Yang Mingyang being denounced, Yang was stripped of his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he joined Minister Tang Jinzhao on an investigative tour of Shaanxi and Sichuan to impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and provincial administration commissioner Li Yiwen; both cases went to strict review. When the inquiry into denunciations against Yang was reopened, Yang was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 金釗留署陝西巡撫。

translations.literal: Tang Jinzhao remained in charge of the Shaanxi governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jinzhao stayed on to administer the Shaanxi governorship.

sentences.zh: 文慶又按河南武陟知縣趙銘彝貪婪狀，劾褫職。

translations.literal: Wen Qing also investigated the greedy conduct of Zhao Mingyi, magistrate of Wuzhi in Henan, and impeached him, resulting in dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing also looked into corruption charges against Zhao Mingyi, magistrate of Wuzhi in Henan, and secured his removal from office.

sentences.zh: 調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the vice ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命在軍機大臣上學習行走，兼右翼總兵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to study and walk in attendance at the Grand Council, concurrently serving as Commander of the Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was assigned to train under the Grand Council and walk in attendance there, while also commanding the Right Wing.

sentences.zh: 命赴熱河，偕都統耆英按歷任總管虧短庫款，褫職追繳。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go to Rehe, and together with Commander-in-chief Qi Ying investigated successive superintendents who had misappropriated treasury funds; they were dismissed and required to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Rehe with Commander-in-chief Qi Ying to audit successive superintendents who had shorted the treasury; the guilty were dismissed and made to repay.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以查辦熱河虧空案內擬罪未晰，召問，奏對失實，下部議，罷直軍機。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, because the assigned penalties in the case of deficits at Rehe were unclear, he was summoned for questioning; his memorial responses were untrue, the matter was referred to the ministry for deliberation, and he was removed from service at the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the penalties proposed in the Rehe deficit case were found unclear; summoned to audience, he answered untruthfully, the matter went to ministerial review, and he was removed from the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 二十年，典江南鄉試，以上下江中額有誤，又私攜湖南舉人熊少牧入闈閱卷，議褫職。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination; because the quota allocation between Upper and Lower Jiang was erroneous, and because he privately brought the Hunan provincial graduate Xiong Shaomu into the examination hall to grade papers, it was decided he should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he served as chief examiner for the Jiangnan provincial tests; errors in the Upper and Lower Jiang quota, together with his smuggling the Hunan graduate Xiong Shaomu into the hall to mark papers, led to a recommendation for dismissal.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，予三等侍衛，充庫倫辦事大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was granted the rank of third-class imperial bodyguard and appointed Commissioner for Affairs at Khüree.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he received third-class imperial bodyguard rank and was appointed commissioner for affairs at Khüree.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，召授吏部侍郎、內務府大臣，連擢左都御史、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and Minister of the Imperial Household, and was promoted in succession to Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was recalled to serve as vice minister of personnel and minister of the Imperial Household, then promoted in quick succession to left censor-in-chief and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，命赴四川，偕總督、將軍按前任駐藏大臣孟保、鍾芳等濫提官物，劾罷之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was ordered to go to Sichuan, and together with the governor-general and the general investigated former Ambans to Tibet Meng Bao, Zhong Fang, and others for abusively requisitioning official goods; they were impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was dispatched to Sichuan with the governor-general and regional general to investigate former Tibetan ambans Meng Bao, Zhong Fang, and others for wrongful requisitions of official property; all were impeached and removed.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，復命為軍機大臣，解內務府事務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was again appointed Grand Councilor and relieved of Imperial Household duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was reappointed to the Grand Council and released from the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 尋署陝甘總督，道經河南，命察賑務，劾玩誤之知縣四人。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu; passing through Henan en route, he was ordered to inspect relief work and impeached four magistrates for negligence.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu; traveling through Henan he was told to inspect famine relief and impeached four magistrates for misconduct and delay.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，召授吏部尚書，兼步軍統領、內務府大臣，罷直軍機處、兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, concurrently Chief Commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie and Minister of the Imperial Household; he ceased service at the Grand Council and concurrently served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was recalled as minister of personnel, concurrently chief of the metropolitan gendarmerie and minister of the Imperial Household; he left the Grand Council while taking on the chancellorship of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三十年，充內大臣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he served as an Inner Court Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he became an inner court minister.

sentences.zh: 薛執中者，甘肅河州人，以符咒惑眾。

translations.literal: Xue Zhizhong was a man of Hezhou in Gansu who deluded the masses with charms and incantations.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Xue Zhizhong, from Hezhou in Gansu, who beguiled crowds with charms and spells.

sentences.zh: 至京師，藉術醫病，朝貴多與往來。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he practiced healing by occult arts, and many high officials associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he treated illness by occult means, and many court grandees sought him out.

sentences.zh: 遂妄議時政，談休咎，行踪詭秘，為巡城御史曹楙堅捕治，中外大臣牽連被譴者眾。

translations.literal: He then presumptuously discussed current affairs and spoke of fortune and misfortune; his movements were secretive. The patrolling censor Cao Moujian arrested and punished him, and many ministers at court and in the provinces were implicated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: He began to meddle in politics and speak of omens, while keeping his movements secret; patrolling censor Cao Moujian seized him, and a host of ministers inside and outside the capital were drawn in and censured.

sentences.zh: 文慶曾延治病，文宗斥其身為步軍統領，不能立時捕究，有乖職守，褫職。

translations.literal: Wen Qing had once invited him to treat an illness. The Wenzong Emperor rebuked him, saying that as Chief Commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie he had failed to arrest and investigate Xue at once, which was a dereliction of duty, and stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing had once called Xue in to treat him. Emperor Xianfeng rebuked him: as chief of the metropolitan gendarmerie he should have seized Xue immediately; by failing to do so he had neglected his office, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，予五品頂戴，辦理昌陵工程。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was granted a fifth-rank peacock feather and put in charge of works at the Changling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he received fifth-rank insignia and supervised construction at the Changling mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 二年，起授內閣學士，尋擢戶部尚書，復為內大臣、翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled and appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, soon promoted to Minister of Revenue, and again made Inner Court Minister and Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled as a grand secretary, soon promoted to minister of revenue, and again made inner court minister and Hanlin chancellor.

sentences.zh: 五年，復為軍機大臣、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again became Grand Councilor and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to the Grand Council as associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 題孝靜皇后神主，加太子太保，拜文淵閣大學士，晉武英殿大學士，管理戶部，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet of Empress Xiaojing was inscribed, he was given the additional title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, placed in charge of the Board of Revenue, and made Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: After inscribing the spirit tablet for Empress Xiaojing he received the additional title grand mentor of the heir apparent, entered the Wenyuan Grand Secretariat, rose to the Wuying Grand Secretariat, took charge of the Board of Revenue, and became chief tutor in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 文慶醇謹持大體，宣宗、文宗知之深，屢躓屢起，眷倚不衰。

translations.literal: Wen Qing was pure, cautious, and upheld the larger principles of governance; the Xuanzong and Wenzong emperors knew him well. Though he stumbled and rose again many times, their favor toward him never waned.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing was upright, careful, and mindful of the larger good; both Daoguang and Xianfeng knew him intimately. Though he fell and was restored again and again, imperial trust in him never faded.

sentences.zh: 時海內多故，粵匪猖熾，欽差大臣賽尚阿、訥爾經額先後以失律被譴。

translations.literal: At the time troubles multiplied throughout the realm; the Cantonese rebels raged fiercely, and the imperial commissioners Sai Shanga and Ne'erjing'e were punished in succession for violations of military discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was beset by troubles; the rebellion in Guangdong burned hot, and imperial commissioners Sai Shanga and Ne'erjing'e were censured one after another for military failures.

sentences.zh: 文慶言：「當重用漢臣，彼多從田間來，知民疾苦，熟諳情偽。

translations.literal: Wen Qing said: "Han Chinese officials ought to be employed in greater numbers. Most of them have come up from the fields; they know the people's hardships and are thoroughly familiar with what is true and false.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing argued: "We should rely more on Han officials. Most of them rose from the countryside; they know the people's suffering and understand what is real and what is not.

sentences.zh: 豈若吾輩未出國門、懵然於大計者乎？」

translations.literal: How can they be compared with us, who have never left the capital gates and remain ignorant of great affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: How does that compare with us, who have never left the capital and remain blind to the larger plan?"

sentences.zh: 常密請破除滿、漢畛域之見，不拘資格以用人。

translations.literal: He often secretly memorialized to break down the barrier between Manchu and Han and to appoint men without being bound by formal qualifications.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly urged in secret memorials that the court set aside Manchu–Han divisions and appoint talent without clinging to seniority and rank.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓初任軍事，屢戰失利，忌者沮抑之。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan first took up military command he suffered repeated defeats in battle, and those who envied him obstructed and held him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan first took the field he lost battle after battle, and jealous rivals worked to hold him down.

sentences.zh: 文慶獨言國籓負時望，能殺賊，終當建非常之功。

translations.literal: Wen Qing alone said that Guofan enjoyed the esteem of the age, could destroy the rebels, and would in the end achieve extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing alone insisted that Guofan commanded public confidence, could destroy the rebels, and would eventually win extraordinary distinction.

sentences.zh: 曾與胡林翼同典試，深知其才略，屢密薦，由貴州道員一歲之間擢至湖北巡撫，凡所奏請，無不從者。

translations.literal: He had once served with Hu Linyi as chief examiner and knew his talent and strategy well; he repeatedly recommended him in secret. Within a single year Hu rose from a circuit intendant in Guizhou to governor of Hubei, and whatever Wen Qing memorialized on his behalf was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Having once served with Hu Linyi as chief examiner, he knew Hu's ability well and recommended him again and again in secret; within a year Hu rose from Guizhou circuit intendant to Hubei governor, and every request Wen Qing made on his behalf was approved.

sentences.zh: 又薦袁甲三、駱秉章之才，請久任勿他調，以觀厥成。

translations.literal: He also recommended the talents of Yuan Jiasan and Luo Bingzhang, asking that they be kept long in their posts without transfer so that their achievements might be seen.
translations.idiomatic: He also commended Yuan Jiasan and Luo Bingzhang and asked that they be left in post without transfer so their work could bear fruit.

sentences.zh: 在戶部，閻敬銘方為主事，當採用其議，非所司者亦諮之。

translations.literal: While at the Board of Revenue, Yan Jingming was then a director; Wen Qing ought to have adopted his proposals, and even matters outside his jurisdiction he consulted him about.
translations.idiomatic: At the Board of Revenue, when Yan Jingming was still a director, Wen Qing took his advice even on matters outside Yan's formal duties.

sentences.zh: 後卒得諸人力以戡定大難。

translations.literal: In the end, through the efforts of these men, the great calamity was suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it was through such men that the great rebellion was put down.

sentences.zh: 端華、肅順漸進用事，皆敬憚其嚴正焉。

translations.literal: As Duanhua and Suishun gradually came to power, both respected and feared his stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Duanhua and Suishun gradually gained power, both respected and feared his stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言各省督撫如慶端、福濟、崇恩、瑛棨等，皆不能勝任，不早罷，恐誤封疆。

translations.literal: In his final memorial he said that governors-general and governors such as Qingduan, Fu Ji, Chong'en, and Yingqi in the various provinces were all unequal to their duties; if they were not dismissed early, he feared the frontiers would be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed memorial warned that governors such as Qingduan, Fu Ji, Chong'en, and Yingqi were unfit for their posts and that delay in removing them would endanger the provinces.

sentences.zh: 文宗深惜之，優詔賜卹，嘉其人品端粹，器量淵深，辦事精勤，通達治體，贈太保，賜金治喪。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor deeply regretted his loss and issued an edict of favor granting mourning benefits, praising his upright character, profound capacity, diligent handling of affairs, and mastery of the principles of governance; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and granted gold for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianfeng mourned him deeply, issued a generous edict of condolence, praised his integrity, depth of mind, diligence, and grasp of statecraft, posthumously made him grand guardian, and granted funds for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 及親奠，見其遺孤幼穉，特詔加恩入祀賢良祠，命其子善聯俟及歲引見；

translations.literal: When the emperor came in person to offer libations and saw that his orphaned children were still young, he issued a special edict of added favor enrolling him in the Shrine of Worthies and ordered his son Shanlian to be presented at court when he reached the proper age;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came in person to mourn and saw how young the orphans were, he specially ordered Wen Qing enrolled in the Shrine of Worthies and directed his son Shanlian to be presented at court when he came of age;

sentences.zh: 弟文玉，以罪遣戍，即釋回。

translations.literal: his younger brother Wenyu, who had been banished for a crime, was immediately released and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: and his younger brother Wenyu, who had been exiled for a crime, was at once released and recalled.

sentences.zh: 予諡文端。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 善聯，官至福州將軍。

translations.literal: Shanlian rose to the post of General at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shanlian rose to serve as general at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 文祥，字博川，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正紅旗人，世居盛京。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang, style name Bochuan, of the Guwalgiya clan, a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner whose family had long resided in Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang, whose style was Bochuan, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan of the Manchu Plain Red Banner; his family had long lived in Mukden.

sentences.zh: 道光二十五年進士，授工部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a director in the Board of Works, and was promoted in succession to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Board of Works as a director, and rose step by step to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，京察，記名道府，因親老，乞留京職。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, at the capital evaluation, he was noted for promotion to circuit intendant or prefect, but because his parents were elderly he begged to remain in a capital post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng the capital evaluation marked him for provincial promotion, but with aged parents at home he asked to stay in a Beijing office.

sentences.zh: 歷太僕寺少卿、詹事、內閣學士，署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and acted as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice director of the Imperial Stud, grand mentor of the heir apparent, and grand secretary, and acted as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 八年，命在軍機大臣上行走，授禮部侍郎，歷吏部、戶部、工部侍郎，兼副都統、左翼總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to walk in attendance at the Grand Council, appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and successively served as Vice Minister of Personnel, Revenue, and Works, concurrently serving as Vice Banner Commander and Commander of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the Grand Council, became vice minister of rites, then served in turn as vice minister of personnel, revenue, and works, while also commanding a banner vice command and the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 十年，英法聯軍犯天津，僧格林沁密疏請幸熱河。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied forces attacked Tianjin, and Senggelinqin submitted a secret memorial asking that the court proceed to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allies advanced on Tianjin, and Senggelinqin secretly urged the court to withdraw to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 文祥以搖動人心，有關大局，且塞外無險可扼，力持不可，偕廷臣言之，復請獨對；

translations.literal: Wen Xiang held that this would shake popular sentiment and concerned the larger situation, and moreover that beyond the passes there were no defensible positions to hold; he strongly maintained that it could not be done, spoke together with court ministers on the matter, and again requested a private audience;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang argued that flight would unsettle the people, touch the fate of the dynasty, and offer no defensible ground beyond the passes; he strongly opposed the move, spoke with other ministers, and again asked for a private audience;

sentences.zh: 退偕同直侍郎匡源、杜翰具疏請罷所調車馬，明詔宣示中外。

translations.literal: after retiring he joined his fellow Grand Council vice ministers Kuang Yuan and Du Han in submitting a memorial asking that the horses and carriages that had been mobilized be dismissed, and that an explicit edict be proclaimed within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: afterward he joined fellow councilors Kuang Yuan and Du Han in a memorial to cancel the mobilized transport and issue a clear edict to reassure the empire.

sentences.zh: 八月，敵氛益熾，車駕遽行，命文祥署步軍統領，司留守。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the enemy threat grew fiercer; the imperial carriage set out in haste, and Wen Xiang was ordered to act as Chief Commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie and oversee those who remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, as the enemy pressed harder, the court fled in haste; Wen Xiang was ordered to act as chief of the metropolitan gendarmerie and oversee those remaining in the capital.

sentences.zh: 從恭親王奕訢議和，出入敵營，於非分之求，侃侃直言，折之以理。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Gong Yixin in negotiating peace, going in and out of the enemy camp; toward improper demands he spoke forthrightly and refuted them with reason.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Prince Gong Yixin in the peace talks, moving in and out of the enemy camps; when unreasonable demands were made, he answered plainly and turned them back with argument.

sentences.zh: 尋以步軍統領難兼顧，疏辭，改署正藍旗護軍統領。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the post of Chief Commandant of the Metropolitan Gendarmerie was hard to combine with his other duties, he memorialized to resign it and was instead appointed acting Commander of the Garrison of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the gendarmerie command too much to combine with his other duties, he asked to be relieved of it and was made acting commander of the Plain Blue Banner garrison.

sentences.zh: 十月，和議成，疏請回鑾，以定人心。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, when the peace agreement was concluded, he memorialized asking that the court return to the capital in order to settle popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, after peace was concluded, he urged the court to return so as to steady public morale.

sentences.zh: 偕恭親王等通籌全局，疏上善後事宜，於是設立總理各國事務衙門，恭親王領之，滿、漢大臣數人，文祥任事最專。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Gong and others he planned the overall situation and memorialized on measures for recovery; thereupon the Office for the General Management of Affairs of All Foreign Countries was established, with Prince Gong at its head and several Manchu and Han ministers; Wen Xiang handled affairs with the greatest dedication.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Gong and others he planned the larger settlement and memorialized on postwar recovery; the Zongli Yamen was then established under Prince Gong with several Manchu and Han ministers, and Wen Xiang shouldered the heaviest share of the work.

sentences.zh: 時和局甫定，發、捻猶熾，兵疲餉竭，近畿空虛。

translations.literal: At the time the peace settlement had only just been made; the Nian and Taiping rebels still raged, the armies were exhausted and funds depleted, and the capital region lay empty.
translations.idiomatic: Peace with the foreigners was barely settled; Nian and Taiping rebels still burned; armies were worn out, funds exhausted, and the capital region lay defenseless.

sentences.zh: 文祥密疏請選練八旗兵丁，添置槍砲，於是始立神機營，尋命管理營務。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang submitted a secret memorial asking that selected and trained Eight Banner troops be chosen and firearms added; thereupon the Shenji Battalion was first established, and he was soon ordered to manage its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang secretly urged that picked Banner troops be drilled and armed with muskets; the Shenji Battalion was founded on this basis, and he was soon put in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 又疏言僧格林沁兵力單薄，勝保所部新募未經行陣。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Senggelinqin's forces were thin, and that the newly recruited troops under Sheng Bao had never seen battle.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Senggelinqin's force was too thin and that Sheng Bao's newly raised men had never been under fire.

sentences.zh: 既恃僧格林沁保障畿輔，必得良將勁卒為贊助，薦副都統富明阿、總兵成明隸其軍；

translations.literal: Since the court relied on Senggelinqin to secure the capital region, good generals and strong soldiers had to be provided as support; he recommended Vice Banner Commander Fuming'a and Brigadier Cheng Ming to serve under his command;
translations.idiomatic: Because the court relied on Senggelinqin to guard the capital approaches, he needed able generals and seasoned troops as support; Wen Xiang recommended Vice Banner Commander Fuming'a and Brigadier Cheng Ming for his army;

sentences.zh: 又薦江西九江道沈葆楨、湖北候補知縣劉蓉堪大用。

translations.literal: he also recommended Shen Baozhen, circuit intendant at Jiujiang in Jiangxi, and Liu Rong, a candidate magistrate in Hubei, as men fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: and he also commended Shen Baozhen, Jiujiang circuit intendant in Jiangxi, and Liu Rong, a candidate magistrate in Hubei, as men of high promise.

sentences.zh: 疏上，並嘉納焉。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, all his recommendations were favorably accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved in full.

sentences.zh: 十一年，文宗崩於熱河行在，穆宗即位，肅順等專政，文祥請解樞務，不許。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Wenzong Emperor died at the traveling palace in Rehe; the Muzong Emperor ascended the throne, and Suishun and his faction monopolized power. Wen Xiang asked to be relieved of Grand Council duties but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Emperor Xianfeng died at the Rehe traveling palace; the Tongzhi Emperor succeeded, and Suishun's faction seized power. Wen Xiang asked to leave the Grand Council but was refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，回鑾，偕王大臣疏請兩宮皇太后垂簾聽政。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, when the court returned to the capital, he joined the princes and ministers in memorializing that the two empress dowagers should rule from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on the return of the court, he joined the princes and ministers in asking that the two empress dowagers rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，連擢左都御史、工部尚書，兼署兵部尚書，為內務府大臣，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted in succession to Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Works, concurrently acting as Minister of War, appointed Minister of the Imperial Household, and made a Banner Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he rose in quick succession to left censor-in-chief and minister of works, acted as minister of war, became minister of the Imperial Household, and took a banner command.

sentences.zh: 二年，管理籓院事務。

translations.literal: In the second year he managed the affairs of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he took charge of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 東南軍事以次戡定，江蘇、浙江省城克復，議加恩樞臣，固辭。

translations.literal: As the southeastern campaigns were suppressed one after another and the provincial capitals of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were recovered, it was proposed to grant added favors to the Grand Councilors; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: As the southeast was pacified step by step and the capitals of Jiangsu and Zhejiang were retaken, rewards for the Grand Council were proposed; he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧复，首逆就殲，捷至，加太子太保，予侄凱肇員外郎。

translations.literal: In the third year Nanjing was recovered and the chief rebel was destroyed; when the victory report arrived, Wen Xiang was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his nephew Kaizhao was granted the post of secretary in the Board.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Nanjing fell and the rebel leader was killed; on news of the victory he received the additional title grand guardian of the heir apparent, and his nephew Kaizhao was made a secretary in the Board.

sentences.zh: 四年，署戶部尚書，辭內務府大臣，允之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he acted as Minister of Revenue, resigned the post of Minister of the Imperial Household, and his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he acted as minister of revenue, resigned from the Imperial Household, and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，馬賊入喜峰口，命文祥率神機營兵防護東陵，督諸軍進剿，賊遁灤陽。

translations.literal: That autumn mounted bandits entered Xifeng Pass; Wen Xiang was ordered to lead Shenji Battalion troops to guard the Eastern Tombs, directed the various armies in pursuit, and the bandits fled to Luanyang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn mounted bandits broke through Xifeng Pass; Wen Xiang was sent with the Shenji Battalion to guard the Eastern Tombs and direct pursuit; the bandits withdrew toward Luanyang.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「地方官豢賊釀患，請除積弊，清盜源。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "Local officials harbor bandits and breed disaster; I ask that accumulated abuses be removed and the sources of banditry cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Local officials shelter bandits and breed trouble; accumulated abuses must be removed and the roots of banditry cut off.

sentences.zh: 馬賊巢穴多在奉天昌圖廳八面城、熱河八溝哈達等處。

translations.literal: The lairs of the mounted bandits are mostly at Bamiancheng in Changtu subprefecture in Fengtian, at Bagou Hada in Rehe, and other such places.
translations.idiomatic: Their strongholds lie chiefly at Bamiancheng in Fengtian's Changtu district, at Bagou Hada in Rehe, and similar places.

sentences.zh: 請購線偵察，調兵掩捕，庶絕根株。」

translations.literal: I ask that informants be hired for reconnaissance and troops be moved to seize them by surprise, so that the roots may be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Hire informants, move troops for surprise arrests, and so destroy them at the root."

sentences.zh: 事定，回京。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 文宗奉安山陵，賜其子熙聯員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor was interred in the imperial mausoleum, his son Xilian was granted the post of secretary in the Board.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianfeng was laid to rest in the imperial tombs, his son Xilian was made a Board secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋以母病請假三月，回旗迎養。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because his mother was ill, he asked for three months' leave and returned to his banner estate to bring her home for care.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, his mother fell ill; he took three months' leave and returned to his banner estate to bring her home.

sentences.zh: 奉天馬賊方熾，命率神機營兵往剿，增調直隸洋槍隊出關，約東三盟蒙古王公由北路夾擊，破賊於錦州東井子。

translations.literal: Mounted bandits in Fengtian were then raging fiercely; he was ordered to lead Shenji Battalion troops to suppress them, with additional detachments of foreign-rifle companies from Zhili sent beyond the passes; he arranged with the Mongol princes of the Eastern Three Leagues to strike from the north, and defeated the bandits at Dongjingzi near Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Fengtian banditry at its height he was ordered out with the Shenji Battalion, reinforced by Zhili foreign-rifle companies beyond the passes; Mongol princes of the Eastern Three Leagues were to strike from the north, and he routed the bandits at Dongjingzi near Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 諜知賊將劫奉天獄，約期攻城，兼程馳援，賊退踞城東南，圍撫順；

translations.literal: Spies reported that the bandits intended to raid the Fengtian prison and had set a date to attack the city; he rushed to the rescue by forced marches. The bandits withdrew to the southeast of the city and besieged Fushun;
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence warned that the bandits would storm the Fengtian jail on a set day; he marched to the rescue at top speed. The bandits fell back southeast of the city and laid siege to Fushun;

sentences.zh: 令總兵劉景芳夜擊破之，賊遁出邊。

translations.literal: he ordered Brigadier Liu Jingfang to attack by night and break them; the bandits fled beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Brigadier Liu Jingfang to break them in a night attack, and the bandits fled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遣軍趨吉林，五年春，解長春廳圍，追賊至昌圖朝陽坡，分三路進擊，十數戰皆捷，擒斬三千餘。

translations.literal: He sent troops toward Jilin; in the spring of the fifth year he relieved the siege of Changchun subprefecture, pursued the bandits to Chaoyang Slope in Changtu, advanced in three columns, won victory in more than ten battles, and captured or killed more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed into Jilin; in the spring of the fifth year he lifted the siege of Changchun, pursued the bandits to Chaoyang Slope in Changtu, attacked in three columns, won a dozen engagements, and killed or captured more than three thousand.

sentences.zh: 賊首馬傻子窮蹙乞降，磔之；

translations.literal: the bandit chief Ma Shazi, hard pressed, begged to surrender and was executed by dismemberment;
translations.idiomatic: The chief Ma Shazi, cornered, begged to surrender and was executed by dismemberment;

sentences.zh: 留兵餉授將軍都興阿，俾清餘孽。

translations.literal: he left troops and funds with General Duxing'a so that the remaining rebels might be cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: he left troops and funds with General Duxing'a to mop up the remnants.

sentences.zh: 請蠲奉天地丁銀米，停鋪捐。

translations.literal: He asked that land-tax silver and grain for Fengtian be remitted and shop levies suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for remission of land tax in silver and grain for Fengtian and an end to shop levies.

sentences.zh: 回京，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Beijing he was made minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 文宗實錄成，賜子熙治員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Wenzong Emperor were completed, his son Xizhi was granted the post of secretary in the Board.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianfeng were completed, his son Xizhi was made a Board secretary.

sentences.zh: 八年，丁母憂，特賜諭祭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered mourning for his mother and was specially granted an edict of condolence sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he went into mourning for his mother and received a special edict of condolence sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 百日假滿，病未出。

translations.literal: When the hundred-day leave expired he was still ill and had not resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred days of mourning ended he was still too ill to return.

sentences.zh: 天津教案起，力疾還朝。

translations.literal: When the Tianjin missionary case arose he returned to court despite his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianjin missionary case broke out he forced himself back to court despite his illness.

sentences.zh: 十年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, as Minister of Personnel, he became Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became associate grand secretary while serving as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 文祥自同治初年偕恭親王同心輔政，總理各國事務，以一身負其責。

translations.literal: From the first years of Tongzhi, Wen Xiang together with Prince Gong assisted in government with one mind, directed affairs of all foreign countries, and bore the responsibility on his own shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: From the early Tongzhi years Wen Xiang worked in concert with Prince Gong, directed foreign affairs, and carried the weight of that charge largely alone.

sentences.zh: 洋情譸幻，朝論紛紜，一以忠信持之，無諉卸。

translations.literal: Foreign affairs were shifting and deceptive, and court opinion was divided; he held to them throughout with loyalty and good faith, without shirking.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign affairs were treacherous and court opinion divided; he met them with steadfast loyalty and never shifted blame.

sentences.zh: 洎穆宗親政，臚陳歷年洋務情形，因應機宜甚備，冀有啟悟。

translations.literal: When the Muzong Emperor personally took up government, he set forth in detail the state of foreign affairs over the years, with measures adapted to circumstances fully prepared, hoping to bring enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi took personal rule, he laid out in full the course of foreign affairs over the years and the measures suited to each turn of events, hoping to open the emperor's eyes.

sentences.zh: 既而恭親王以阻圓明園工程忤旨斥罷，文祥涕泣，偕同列力諫，幾同譴。

translations.literal: Soon after, Prince Gong was dismissed for offending the imperial will by blocking work on the Old Summer Palace; Wen Xiang wept, joined his colleagues in strenuous remonstrance, and nearly shared in the reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Prince Gong was dismissed for defying the throne by opposing restoration of the Old Summer Palace. Wen Xiang wept and, with his colleagues, remonstrated so forcefully that he nearly suffered the same punishment.

sentences.zh: 恭親王尋復職，而自屢遭挫折後，任事不能如初。

translations.literal: Prince Gong was soon restored to office, but after repeated setbacks he could no longer serve affairs as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong was soon reinstated, but after so many reversals he could no longer work with his former energy.

sentences.zh: 文祥正色立朝，為中外所嚴憚，朝局賴以維持，不致驟變。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang stood sternly at court and was held in awe at home and abroad; the court situation relied on him to be maintained and did not change suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang held himself with stern dignity at court and was deeply respected at home and abroad. The court leaned on him to keep steady and avoid sudden upheaval.

sentences.zh: 十三年，病久不瘉，在告，會日本窺台灣，強出籌戰守。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his illness long uncured, he was on leave; it happened that Japan cast eyes on Taiwan, and he forced himself out to plan war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, still ill and on leave, he forced himself back to duty when Japan threatened Taiwan and drew up plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 疏請：「敕下戶部、內務府寬籌餉需，裁減浮用，停不急之工作，謀至急之海防，俾部臣、疆臣皆得專力圖維。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested: "Let an edict go down to the Board of Revenue and the Imperial Household Department to broadly raise funds, cut superfluous expenses, halt work that is not urgent, and plan coastal defense that is most urgent, so that ministry officials and frontier officials may all devote their strength to preservation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Order the Board of Revenue and the Imperial Household Department to raise funds generously, cut wasteful spending, suspend nonessential projects, and devote resources to urgent coastal defense, so ministers and provincial governors can focus on keeping the realm intact.

sentences.zh: 皇上憂勤惕厲，斯內外臣工不敢蹈玩洩之習。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is anxious, diligent, and vigilant, then inner and outer officials will not dare follow habits of laxity and neglect.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty remains anxious, diligent, and vigilant, officials at court and in the provinces will not lapse into complacency.

sentences.zh: 否則狃以為安，不思變計，恐中外解體，人心動搖，其患有不可勝言者。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, accustomed to taking things as secure and not thinking to change plans, I fear the realm at home and abroad may disintegrate and popular sentiment shake; the calamities are beyond what can be told."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, taking false comfort and refusing to change course, the empire may come apart and popular loyalty may waver—with consequences too grave to describe."

sentences.zh: 言甚切至。

translations.literal: His words were very earnest and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: His language was urgent and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，穆宗崩，德宗繼統即位，晉武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: That winter Emperor Muzong died; Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne and took office, and Wen Xiang was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Tongzhi died and Emperor Guangxu ascended the throne; Wen Xiang was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 以久病請罷，溫詔慰留，解諸兼職，專任軍機大臣及總理各國事務。

translations.literal: Because of long illness he asked to resign; a warm edict comforted and retained him, relieved him of various concurrent posts, and charged him solely as Grand Councilor and director of the General Management of Affairs of All Foreign Countries.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on account of chronic illness; a gracious edict kept him in service, stripped him of other concurrent posts, and left him solely as grand councilor and head of foreign affairs at the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 時國家漸多故，文祥深憂之，密陳大計疏曰：「洋人為患中國，愈久愈深，而其窺伺中國之間，亦愈熟愈密。

translations.literal: At that time the state gradually had many troubles; Wen Xiang deeply worried over them and in a secret memorial on the great plan said: "Foreigners as a calamity to China grow the longer the deeper, and their watching for openings in China also grows the more practiced and the more close.
translations.idiomatic: As troubles multiplied, Wen Xiang grew deeply alarmed and submitted a secret memorial on grand strategy: "The foreign menace to China grows deeper with time, and their search for openings in China grows ever more practiced and relentless.

sentences.zh: 從前屢戰屢和，迄無定局，因在事諸臣操縱未宜。

translations.literal: From former times there were repeated wars and repeated peace, yet to the end no settled pattern, because the officials in charge did not handle matters properly.
translations.idiomatic: For years we fought and made peace by turns without ever reaching a stable settlement, because those in charge mishandled affairs.

sentences.zh: 及庚申定約，設立衙門專司其事，以至於今，未見決裂。

translations.literal: When the Gengshen treaty was fixed and a yamen was established to specialize in these matters, down to today no rupture has been seen.
translations.idiomatic: After the treaties of the 1860 crisis and the founding of a dedicated office for foreign affairs, relations have held—so far without open rupture.

sentences.zh: 就事論事，固當相機盡心辦理，而揣洋人之用心，求馭外之大本，則不繫於此，所繫者在人心而已矣。

translations.literal: Judging matters as matters, one should indeed seize the moment and handle them with full heart; but considering foreigners' intent and seeking the great root of governing outsiders, it does not depend on this—the dependence is on popular sentiment alone.
translations.idiomatic: Day-to-day business must still be handled conscientiously as circumstances allow; but if we read foreign intentions and seek the true foundation for managing them, that foundation lies not in procedure but in the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 溯自嘉慶年間，洋人漸形強悍，始而海島，繼而口岸，再及內地，蓄力厲精習機器，以待中國之間，一逞其欲。

translations.literal: Tracing back from the Jiaqing years, foreigners gradually showed fierceness: first on sea islands, then at treaty ports, then reaching the interior; they stored strength, sharpened skill, studied machines, and waited for an opening in China to give full vent to their desires.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jiaqing reign foreigners have grown steadily bolder—first on offshore islands, then at treaty ports, then inland—training troops, mastering machinery, and waiting for a crack in China through which to press their ambitions.

sentences.zh: 道光年間，肆掠江、浙，自江寧換約以後，覬覦觀望。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang years they rampaged through Jiangsu and Zhejiang; after the treaty exchange at Jiangning they watched and coveted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang they ravaged the lower Yangzi; after the Nanjing treaty they watched and waited for their chance.

sentences.zh: 直至粵匪滋事，以為中國有此犯上作亂之事，人心不一，得其間矣。

translations.literal: Until the Guangdong bandits stirred trouble, they thought China had this matter of rebellion against superiors and disorder, popular hearts not united—they had gained their opening.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiping rebellion broke out they judged that China was torn by rebellion and divided in loyalty—and that their opening had come.

sentences.zh: 於是其謀遂洩，闖入津門，雖經小挫，而其意愈堅，致有庚申之警。

translations.literal: Thereupon their plot was revealed; they burst into the Tianjin gates; though they met small setbacks, their intent grew firmer, leading to the alarm of Gengshen.
translations.idiomatic: Their designs then came into the open: they forced the Tianjin approaches, and though checked briefly, pressed on until the crisis of 1860.

sentences.zh: 然其時勢局固危，民心未二，勤王之師雖非勁旅，而聞警偕來；

translations.literal: Yet at that time the situation was indeed perilous, popular hearts were not divided, and though the armies that came to aid the throne were not crack troops, on hearing the alarm they came together;
translations.idiomatic: The situation was dire, yet the people had not turned against the throne; relief armies were not elite troops, but they rallied when the alarm sounded;

sentences.zh: 奸細之徒雖被誘脅，而公憤同具，以是得受羈縻，成此和局。

translations.literal: traitorous elements though enticed and coerced, yet shared public outrage was alike present; by this they were able to be held in restraint and this peace settlement was formed.
translations.idiomatic: and though spies were suborned, public outrage was united. On that basis the foreigners could be held in restraint and the present peace settlement was formed.

sentences.zh: 十餘年來，仰賴皇太后、皇上勵精圖治，宵旰勤勞，無間隙之可尋；

translations.literal: For more than ten years, relying on the Empress Dowager and Your Majesty exerting spirit to govern well, toiling from dawn to dusk, no gap could be found;
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade the realm has relied on the empress dowager and Your Majesty ruling with tireless diligence, leaving no opening for exploit;

sentences.zh: 在事諸臣始得遇事維持，未至啟釁，偶有乾求，尚能往返爭持，不至太甚，非洋務之順手，及在事者折沖之力，皆我皇太后、皇上朝乾夕惕，事事期符民隱，人心固結，有以折外族之心，而杜未形之患也。

translations.literal: officials in charge could then meet affairs and maintain them, not reach the point of provoking conflict; when occasionally there were demands, they could still go back and forth in contention and not reach excess—not because foreign affairs went smoothly or because those in charge had the power to parry, but all because our Empress Dowager and Your Majesty are vigilant morning and evening, in every matter expecting to accord with the people's hidden wishes, popular hearts firmly bound, having means to bend the hearts of foreign tribes and stop troubles not yet formed.
translations.idiomatic: so that officials handling foreign affairs could hold the line, avoid provocation, and even push back on unreasonable demands. That is not because foreign policy has gone smoothly or because negotiators have been unusually skillful, but because Your Majesty and the empress dowager have ruled with constant vigilance, aligned policy with the people's wishes, and kept popular loyalty firm—thereby restraining foreign ambition and heading off dangers before they appear.

sentences.zh: 然而各國火器技藝之講求益進，彼此相結之勢益固。

translations.literal: Yet each country's pursuit of firearms and craft advances daily, and the tendency of mutual alliance grows firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every power advances further in arms and technology, and their alliances grow tighter.

sentences.zh: 使臣久駐京師，聞我一政之當則憂，一或不當則喜，其探測愈精。

translations.literal: Envoys long stationed in the capital hear one policy of ours that is right and worry, one that is not right and rejoice; their probing grows more precise.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys long resident in Beijing rejoice when we misstep and worry when we govern well; their scrutiny grows ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 俄人逼於西疆，法人計佔越南，緊接滇、粵，英人謀由印度入藏及蜀，蠢蠢欲動之勢，益不可遏。

translations.literal: Russians press on the western frontier, French plan to seize Vietnam adjoining Yunnan and Guangdong, English plot from India into Tibet and Shu—the restless stirring tendency grows ever harder to check.
translations.idiomatic: Russia presses the western frontier; France schemes at Vietnam on Yunnan and Guangdong's border; Britain eyes Tibet and Sichuan from India. Restless aggression grows harder to contain by the day.

sentences.zh: 所伺者中國之間耳，所惎者中國大本之未搖，而人心之難違耳。

translations.literal: What they watch for is only an opening in China; what they fear is only that China's great foundation has not shaken and that popular hearts are hard to defy.
translations.idiomatic: They wait only for an opening in China; what restrains them is that the dynasty's foundation has not yet shaken and that the people's will cannot easily be defied.

sentences.zh: 說者謂各國性近犬羊，未知政治，然其國中偶有動作，必由其國主付上議院議之，所謂謀及卿士也；

translations.literal: Some say the various countries are by nature like dogs and sheep and do not understand government; yet when occasionally there is action in their states, it must be referred by their sovereign to the upper house for deliberation—what is called consulting the high ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Some dismiss the powers as barbarous and ignorant of government; yet when their rulers act, they refer matters to the upper house—what the classics call consulting the high ministers;

sentences.zh: 付下議院議之，所謂謀及庶人也。

translations.literal: referred to the lower house for deliberation—what is called consulting the common people.
translations.idiomatic: and to the lower house—consulting the common people.

sentences.zh: 議之可行則行，否則止，事事必合乎民情而後決然行之。

translations.literal: If deliberation finds it feasible they act; if not they stop; in every matter they must accord with popular sentiment before resolutely carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: What passes deliberation they enact; what fails they drop. Nothing is done until it aligns with popular sentiment.

sentences.zh: 自治其國以此，其觀他國之廢興成敗亦以此。

translations.literal: They govern their own countries by this, and they view other countries' decline, rise, success, and failure also by this.
translations.idiomatic: They govern themselves by this standard, and they judge other nations' rise and fall by it as well.

sentences.zh: 儻其國一切政治皆與民情相背，則各國始逞所欲為，取之恐後矣。

translations.literal: If a country's every policy runs against popular sentiment, then the various countries begin to give full play to what they wish and seize it, fearing to be late.
translations.idiomatic: When a state's policies run against its people, the powers rush to exploit it, each fearing to arrive too late.

sentences.zh: 如土耳其、希臘等國，勢極弱小，而得以久存各大國之間者，其人心固也。

translations.literal: Such as Turkey, Greece, and other countries—extremely weak in power—yet able long to survive among the great powers: their popular hearts are firm.
translations.idiomatic: Turkey and Greece are very weak yet endure among the great powers because their peoples remain united.

sentences.zh: 強大如法國，而德國得以勝之者，以法王窮侈任性，負國債之多不可復計，雖日益額餉以要結兵心，而民心已去，始有以乘其間也。

translations.literal: Mighty as France, yet Germany was able to overcome it—because the French king was extravagant to exhaustion and willful, national debt beyond reckoning; though daily increasing pay to bind soldiers' hearts, popular hearts had already departed, and only then was there means to seize the opening.
translations.idiomatic: France was mighty, yet Germany defeated it because the French king lived in ruinous luxury, piled up unpayable debt, and tried to buy the army with ever higher pay while losing the people—giving Germany its opening.

sentences.zh: 夫人必自侮而後人侮之，物必先自腐而後蟲生焉。

translations.literal: A man must first insult himself and afterward others insult him; a thing must first rot itself and afterward worms are born.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who despise themselves are despised by others; only what rots from within breeds worms.

sentences.zh: 理之所在，勢所必至。

translations.literal: Where principle lies, tendency necessarily arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the logic of events; such is what must follow.

sentences.zh: 中國之有外國，猶人身之有疾病，病者必相證用藥，而培元氣為尤要。

translations.literal: China having foreigners is like the human body having illness; the ill must be treated with medicine suited to symptoms, yet nourishing the vital energy is especially important.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign powers afflicting China are like disease afflicting the body: symptoms must be treated, but strengthening the body's vital force matters most.

sentences.zh: 外國無日不察我民心之向背，中國必求無事不愜於民心之是非。

translations.literal: Foreign countries have no day on which they do not examine whether our popular hearts turn toward or away; China must seek that in no matter it fail to satisfy the people's right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners watch daily whether the people stand with or against the throne; China must ensure that nothing we do offends popular judgment of right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 中國天澤分嚴，外國上議院、下議院之設，勢有難行，而義可採取。

translations.literal: In China heaven's favor and rank are sharply divided; establishing foreign upper and lower houses would be hard in tendency, yet the principle may be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: China's hierarchy of imperial grace is strict; we cannot simply copy foreign parliaments, but we can adopt their underlying principle.

sentences.zh: 凡我用人行政，一舉一動，揆之至理，度之民情，非人心所共愜，則急止勿為；

translations.literal: In all our employment of men and administration of affairs, every move and act—measure to utmost principle, estimate against popular sentiment; what popular hearts do not together find pleasing, then urgently stop and do not do;
translations.idiomatic: In appointing officials and governing, every act should be weighed against principle and popular sentiment; what the people cannot accept should be stopped at once;

sentences.zh: 事係人心所共快，則務期於成。

translations.literal: matters that concern what popular hearts together rejoice in, then strive to bring to completion.
translations.idiomatic: and what the people wholeheartedly support should be carried through to success.

sentences.zh: 崇節儉以裕帑需，遇事始能有備，納諫諍以開言路，下情藉以上通。

translations.literal: Uphold frugality to enrich treasury needs, so that when affairs come there may be preparation; accept remonstrance to open the path of speech, so lower sentiments may thereby reach above.
translations.idiomatic: Practice frugality to fill the treasury and prepare for emergencies; welcome remonstrance to open channels so grievances from below reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 總期人心永結，大本永固，當各外國環伺之時，而使之無一間可乘，庶彼謀不能即遂，而在我亦堪自立。

translations.literal: In sum expect popular hearts forever bound and the great foundation forever firm; when the various foreign countries encircle and watch, cause them to have not one opening to exploit—then perhaps their plots cannot immediately succeed, and on our side we may also stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: Keep popular loyalty firm and the dynasty's foundation secure, so that while foreign powers circle they find no opening—their designs may fail, and China may still stand on its own.

sentences.zh: 此為目前猶可及之計，亦為此時不能稍緩之圖。

translations.literal: This is a plan still attainable at present, and also a design that at this time cannot be slightly delayed.
translations.idiomatic: This is a course still within reach—and one that brooks no delay.

sentences.zh: 若待其間之既開，而欲為斡旋補苴之法，則和與戰俱不可恃。

translations.literal: If one waits until the opening is already made and then wishes to apply mediating, patching methods, then both peace and war are alike unreliable.
translations.idiomatic: Once the opening appears, neither negotiation nor war can be relied on.

sentences.zh: 即使仍可苟安，而大局已不堪復問，則何如預防其間之為計也。

translations.literal: Even if one could still scrape by in security, the great situation would already be beyond asking again—how much better to plan by preventing the opening beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Even temporary safety would leave the larger situation beyond repair. How much better to prevent the opening before it comes.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年王茂廕奏陳夷務，謂：'海外諸國日起爭雄，自人視之，雖有中外之分，自天視之，殆無彼此之意。'

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on barbarian affairs, saying: 'Overseas countries daily rise to contend for supremacy; viewed by men, though there is division of China and abroad, viewed by Heaven, probably there is no intent of this and that.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on foreign affairs, saying: 'Overseas powers contend daily for dominance; men see a line between China and abroad, but Heaven may see no such distinction.'

sentences.zh: 引書言'皇天無親，惟德是輔'，及大學平天下章三言得失，首人心、次天命、而終以君心為證。

translations.literal: He cited the Classic: 'High Heaven has no partiality; it assists only virtue,' and the Great Learning chapter on bringing peace to the world, which thrice speaks of gain and loss—first popular hearts, next Heaven's mandate, and finally taking the ruler's heart as proof.
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the Classic—'High Heaven has no favorites; it aids only the virtuous'—and the Great Learning on ordering the realm, which three times names the sources of success and failure: first the people's hearts, then Heaven's mandate, and finally the ruler's own heart as proof.

sentences.zh: 何其言之危且切歟！

translations.literal: How perilous and urgent his words!
translations.idiomatic: How grave and urgent his warning was!

sentences.zh: 欲戢夷心，莫要於順民心，能順民心，斯足以承天心，固不待蓍蔡而昭然若睹耳。

translations.literal: To restrain barbarian hearts, nothing is more essential than following popular hearts; able to follow popular hearts, that suffices to receive Heaven's heart—indeed without need of divination by yarrow or milfoil it is clear as if seen.
translations.idiomatic: To quiet foreign ambition, nothing matters more than winning the people's hearts; win the people and you win Heaven's favor—no divination needed to see that truth.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩最重，辦理洋務最久，實有見於洋人居心積慮之處，而現時尤為迫切緊要之關。

translations.literal: Your servant has received grace most heavily and handled foreign affairs longest; I truly have insight into where foreigners harbor intent and long plotting, and at present this is especially the urgent, critical hinge.
translations.idiomatic: I have received the deepest favor and handled foreign affairs longer than any other minister; I have seen where foreigners scheme, and I know this moment is the critical hinge.

sentences.zh: 外國之求間在此，中國之彌間亦在此。

translations.literal: Foreign countries' seeking of openings lies here; China's closing of openings also lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Foreigners seek their opening here; China must close it here.

sentences.zh: 在事諸臣，僅謀其末，我皇上實操其本。

translations.literal: Officials in charge only plot the branches; Your Majesty truly holds the root.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in charge can manage only details; Your Majesty holds the root in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 用敢直陳，伏乞俯鑑芻言，將此摺時置左右，力求端本之治，以回隱患之萌。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare speak plainly, prostrate and beg Your Majesty to look down and discern these humble words, place this memorial often at your side, strive for government that rectifies the root, and turn back the sprouting of hidden calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore speak plainly and beg Your Majesty to heed these humble words, keep this memorial close at hand, and pursue government that heals the root—before hidden dangers take hold.

sentences.zh: 天下幸甚！」

translations.literal: Great fortune for the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: The realm would be blessed indeed!"

sentences.zh: 先是，當台灣事平，文祥即偕恭親王議興海防，條上六事：曰練兵，曰簡器，曰造船，曰籌餉，曰用人，曰持久。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Taiwan affair was settled, Wen Xiang at once joined Prince Gong in discussing the promotion of coastal defense and listed six items in memorial: namely training troops, selecting arms, building ships, raising funds, employing men, and endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Taiwan crisis ended, Wen Xiang and Prince Gong had proposed coastal defense in six points: train troops, improve arms, build ships, raise funds, appoint the right men, and sustain the effort over time.

sentences.zh: 各具條目，敕下中外大臣會議。

translations.literal: Each had detailed items; an edict was sent down for Chinese and foreign ministers to confer.
translations.idiomatic: Each point was spelled out in detail, and an edict ordered court and provincial officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 至光緒二年，疆臣覆奏，將復下廷議。

translations.literal: By the second year of Guangxu frontier officials had replied in memorial and the matter was to be sent down again for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Guangxu the governors had reported back, and the proposals were to go before the court again.

sentences.zh: 文祥已病不能出，自知且不起，乃密疏上曰：「馭外之端，為國家第一要務。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang was already ill and could not go out; knowing himself about not to rise again, he then submitted a secret memorial saying: "The handling of outsiders is the state's first essential matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was too ill to leave his house and knew he would not recover. He submitted a secret memorial: "Managing foreign powers is the state's foremost duty.

sentences.zh: 現籌自強之計，為安危全局一大關鍵。

translations.literal: The plan now being drawn for self-strengthening is a great hinge of safety and peril for the whole situation.
translations.idiomatic: The self-strengthening program now under discussion is the key to the empire's survival.

sentences.zh: 臣衰病侵尋，心長智短，知不能永效犬馬以報主知。

translations.literal: Your servant's declining illness presses on; my heart is long but my wisdom short; I know I cannot forever serve like dog or horse to repay my lord's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: My strength fails and my wits grow short; I know I cannot long serve as Your Majesty's loyal hound.

sentences.zh: 恐一旦填溝壑，則平生欲言未言之隱，無以上達宸聰，下資會議，何以對陛下？

translations.literal: I fear that once I fill gullies and ravines, then life's hidden matters I wished to speak but did not speak cannot reach above to the imperial ear or aid below the conference—how may I face Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If I should die, the truths I have kept silent will never reach Your Majesty's ear or inform the coming deliberations. How could I face you then?

sentences.zh: 此心耿耿，有非總理衙門原奏所能盡者，敢竭誠吐赤，為我皇上敬陳之。

translations.literal: This loyal heart has what the Zongli Yamen's original memorial cannot fully express; I dare exhaust sincerity and speak my red heart, respectfully setting it forth for my Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: My loyal heart holds more than the Zongli Yamen's original memorial could say; I offer these words in full sincerity for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 夫敵國外患，無代無之，然未有如今日之局之奇、患之深、為我敵者之多且狡也。

translations.literal: Enemy states and foreign calamity—no age lacks them; yet never has there been a situation as strange as today's, calamity as deep, or enemies as many and cunning toward us.
translations.idiomatic: Every age has foreign enemies, but never a situation as strange, a peril as deep, or foes as numerous and cunning as today.

sentences.zh: 果因此患而衡慮困心，自立不敗，原足作我精神，惺我心志，厲我志氣，所謂生於憂患者正在於此。

translations.literal: If truly because of this calamity one weighs cares and troubles the heart, stands firm without defeat, it can fully rouse our spirit, awaken our resolve, and sharpen our will—what is called being born in worry and calamity is precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: If we meet this peril with sober resolve and stand firm, it can rouse our spirit, awaken our minds, and steel our will—this is what the sages meant by strength born of adversity.

sentences.zh: 至此而復因循洩沓；

translations.literal: To reach this point and again be dilatory and lax;
translations.idiomatic: Yet if at this point we lapse into delay and negligence;

sentences.zh: 一聽諸數而莫為之籌，即偶一籌念而移時輒忘，或有名無實，大局將不堪設想，而其幾不待智者而決矣。

translations.literal: letting everything drift with no planning, or even if occasionally there is a thought of planning yet after a time it is forgotten, or there is name without reality—the great situation will be beyond imagining, and its outcome needs no wise man to decide.
translations.idiomatic: if we leave matters to drift, forget plans as soon as they are made, or pursue empty forms without substance, the consequences are unthinkable—and the outcome needs no sage to predict.

sentences.zh: 從前夷患之熾，由於中外之情相隔，和戰之見無定，疆吏又遇事粉飾，其情形不能上達於朝廷。

translations.literal: Formerly the fierceness of barbarian calamity arose because sentiment at home and abroad was separated, views on peace and war had no fixity, and frontier officials on meeting affairs prettified them so conditions could not reach the court.
translations.idiomatic: Past foreign crises grew fierce because court and provinces were estranged, policy swung between peace and war without settled principle, and frontier officials whitewashed reports so the throne never learned the truth.

sentences.zh: 坐是三失，而其患遂日久日深，無所底止。

translations.literal: Sitting in these three losses, the calamity then grew day by day deeper with no bottom or stop.
translations.idiomatic: These three failures fed one another, and the trouble deepened day by day without end.

sentences.zh: 泰西各國官商一氣，政教並行，各商舶遠涉重洋，初至中華，處處受我侮抑，事事被我阻塞，其情鬱而不能不發者，勢也。

translations.literal: Western countries' officials and merchants are of one breath, government and teaching proceed together; each merchant ship crossing the far ocean, on first reaching China, everywhere received our insult and suppression, every matter was blocked by us—their sentiment pent up and unable not to burst forth: such was tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Western states unite officials and merchants, church and state. Their traders crossed the oceans to China and everywhere met insult and obstruction; resentment had to break out—that was the logic of events.

sentences.zh: 繼而見中國官之阻之者可以通，抑之者可以伸，必不可破之格，或取勝於兵力之相迫而卒無不破，此中國之為所輕而各國漸敢恣肆之機也。

translations.literal: Then they saw that what Chinese officials blocked could be opened, what they suppressed could be extended, rules that must not be broken—or won by pressure of armed force—ultimately had none unbroken: this was the occasion for China to be held light and the various countries gradually to dare license.
translations.idiomatic: They then learned that every Chinese barrier could be forced open, every prohibition reversed, every 'iron rule' broken—often by the threat of arms. That was when they began to despise China and grow bold.

sentences.zh: 迨至立約通商已有成議，而內無深知洋務之大臣，在外無究心撫馭之疆吏，一切奏牘之陳，類多敷衍諱飾。

translations.literal: When treaties for trade were established and agreements made, yet within there were no grand ministers who deeply understood foreign affairs, and outside no frontier officials who devoted heart to pacifying and controlling—all memorials submitted were mostly perfunctory and concealing.
translations.idiomatic: Treaties were signed and trade opened, yet at court no minister truly understood foreign affairs, and in the provinces no governor devoted himself to managing them. Memorials were mostly evasive and cosmetic.

sentences.zh: 敵人方桀驁而稱為恭順，洋情方怨毒而號為懽忭，遂至激成事端，忽和忽戰；

translations.literal: Enemies were just arrogant while called submissive; foreign sentiment was just resentful and poisonous while proclaimed joyful—thus matters were stirred to incidents, suddenly peace and suddenly war;
translations.idiomatic: Enemies were called obedient while still defiant; foreign resentment was reported as goodwill—until crises erupted and policy lurched between peace and war;

sentences.zh: 甚且彼省之和局甫成，此省之戰事又起，賠款朝給，捷書暮陳。

translations.literal: even to the point that peace in that province was just settled when war in this province rose again; indemnities paid in the morning, victory reports submitted at evening.
translations.idiomatic: peace might be signed in one province while fighting broke out in another; indemnities were paid by day and false victory reports filed by night.

sentences.zh: 乘遭風之船以為勝仗，執送信之酋以為擒渠，果至兩軍相交，仍復一敗不可收拾。

translations.literal: Taking a ship that met wind as a victorious battle, seizing a chief who came bearing letters as capturing the ringleader—when truly the two armies met, again one defeat beyond gathering up.
translations.idiomatic: A storm-struck ship was claimed as a great victory; a messenger was hailed as a captured enemy chief—yet when armies actually clashed, defeat was total.

sentences.zh: 於是夷情愈驕，約款愈肆，中外大臣皆視辦理洋務為畏途，而庚申釁起，幾至無可措手。

translations.literal: Thereupon barbarian sentiment grew prouder, treaty terms more wanton; Chinese and foreign grand ministers all viewed handling foreign affairs as a road of fear, and the Gengshen trouble rose, nearly reaching the point of no hand able to act.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign arrogance and treaty demands grew worse; ministers at court and in the provinces alike dreaded foreign affairs—until the 1860 crisis left the government almost helpless.

sentences.zh: 自設立總理衙門，其事始有責成，情形漸能熟悉，在事諸臣亦無敢推諉。

translations.literal: From establishing the Zongli Yamen, its affairs began to have fixed responsibility; conditions gradually could be known familiarly, and officials in charge also did not dare shirk.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zongli Yamen was founded, responsibility was clear, officials grew familiar with foreign affairs, and those in charge could no longer pass the buck.

sentences.zh: 然其事非在事諸臣之事，而國家切要之事也。

translations.literal: Yet these affairs are not the affairs of officials in charge alone, but matters urgently essential to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet foreign affairs are not the private business of a few officials—they are vital to the state itself.

sentences.zh: 既為國家切要之事，則凡為大清臣子者，無人不應一心謀畫，以維大局。

translations.literal: Since they are urgently essential state matters, then all who are subjects of the Great Qing should, with none excluded, unite heart in planning to preserve the great situation.
translations.idiomatic: If they are vital to the state, every subject of the Qing ought to devote himself to preserving the larger order.

sentences.zh: 況和局之本在自強，自強之要在武備，亦非總理衙門所能操其權盡其用也。

translations.literal: Moreover the root of a peace settlement lies in self-strengthening; the essentials of self-strengthening lie in military preparedness—nor can the Zongli Yamen alone wield its authority and exhaust its use.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, lasting peace rests on self-strengthening, and self-strengthening rests on real military power—matters the Zongli Yamen cannot control or carry out alone.

sentences.zh: 使武備果有實際，則於外族要求之端，持之易力，在彼有顧忌，覦覬亦可潛消，事不盡屬總理衙門，而無事不息息相關也。

translations.literal: If military preparedness truly has substance, then on points of foreign tribes' demands holding them is easier in strength; on their side there is apprehension, coveting also may quietly dissolve—affairs do not all belong to the Zongli Yamen, yet in no matter is there not breath linked to breath.
translations.idiomatic: With real armed strength, foreign demands can be resisted more effectively, rivals will hesitate, and covetous designs may fade—though not every matter falls to the Yamen, nothing is unrelated to it.

sentences.zh: 乃十數年來，遇有重大之端，安危呼吸之際，事外諸臣以袖手為得計；

translations.literal: Yet for more than ten years, when major issues arose, at moments when safety and peril hung on a breath, officials outside the matter took folding arms as the winning plan;
translations.idiomatic: Yet for more than a decade, whenever crisis struck and the realm hung in the balance, officials outside the foreign-affairs circle treated standing aside as the wise course;

sentences.zh: 事甫就緒，異議復生，或轉託於成事不說；

translations.literal: when affairs were just settled, dissent arose again, or blame was shifted with the saying that success needs no explanation;
translations.idiomatic: and when a settlement neared, dissent revived, or critics invoked the proverb that victors need not explain themselves;

sentences.zh: 不問事之難易情形若何，一歸咎於任事之人。

translations.literal: without asking how difficult the matter or what the situation, blame was wholly placed on those charged with the task.
translations.idiomatic: without regard for difficulty or circumstance, blaming only those who bore responsibility.

sentences.zh: 是從前之誤以無專責而仔肩乏人，今日之事又以有專屬而藉口有自。

translations.literal: Thus formerly the error was that with no fixed responsibility no one shouldered the burden; today's affairs again use the fact of a fixed assignment as pretext that blame has a source.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fault was that no one was clearly in charge; now the fault is that a dedicated office gives everyone else an excuse to shift blame.

sentences.zh: 設在事諸臣亦同存此心，爭相諉謝，必至如唐臣杜甫詩中所謂'獨使至尊憂社稷'矣。

translations.literal: Suppose officials in charge also harbored this heart and vied to shirk and decline—one would necessarily reach what the Tang official Du Fu's poem calls 'leaving the Son of Heaven alone to worry over the altars of state.'
translations.idiomatic: If those in charge shared that attitude and shirked together, we would arrive at Du Fu's lament: 'Only the Son of Heaven is left to worry for the realm.'

sentences.zh: 夫能戰始能守，能守始能和，宜人人知之。

translations.literal: To be able to fight is first to be able to defend; to be able to defend is first to be able to make peace—this all should know.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who can fight can hold; only those who can hold can make peace. That should be common knowledge.

sentences.zh: 今日之敵，非得其所長，斷難與抗，稍識時務者，亦詎勿知？

translations.literal: Today's enemies—unless one obtains what they excel in, it is hard in the extreme to resist them; those who slightly know the times—how could they not know?
translations.idiomatic: Today's foes cannot be resisted without mastering their own strengths. Whoever understands the times knows that.

sentences.zh: 乃至緊要關鍵，意見頓相背，往往陳義甚高，鄙洋務為不足言，抑或苟安為計，覺和局之深可恃。

translations.literal: Yet at the critical hinge opinions suddenly oppose: often principles are set forth very high and foreign affairs are despised as unworthy of speech, or else taking false security as plan, feeling the peace settlement deeply reliable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the decisive moment opinions divide: some speak in lofty moral terms and dismiss foreign affairs as beneath discussion; others seek a false peace and trust too deeply in the present settlement.

sentences.zh: 是以歷來練兵、造船、習器、天文、算學諸事，每興一議而阻之者多，即就一事而為之者非其實。

translations.literal: Therefore through the ages in training troops, building ships, practicing arms, astronomy, and mathematics—each time one matter was raised, those who blocked were many; even when one matter was undertaken, what was done was not real.
translations.idiomatic: Hence every proposal to train troops, build ships, study arms, astronomy, or mathematics has met heavy obstruction; even when approved, execution has often been hollow.

sentences.zh: 至於無成，則不咎其阻撓之故，而責創議之人；

translations.literal: When there was no success, they did not blame the reason of obstruction but blamed those who originated the proposal;
translations.idiomatic: When projects failed, critics blamed not those who blocked them but those who proposed them;

sentences.zh: 甚至局外紛紛論說，以國家經營自立之計，而指為敷衍洋人。

translations.literal: even to the point that outsiders talked in confusion, taking the state's plans for self-reliance and calling them perfunctory service to foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: and outsiders even denounced the state's plans for self-reliance as groveling to foreigners.

sentences.zh: 所見之誤，竟至於此！

translations.literal: The error of views actually reached this point!
translations.idiomatic: Judgment had sunk to that depth!

sentences.zh: 今日本擾台之役業經議結，日本尚非法、英、俄、美之比，此事本屬無名之師，已幾幾震動全局，費盡筆爭舌戰，始就範圍。
