translations.literal: Now Japan's disturbance of Taiwan has already been settled by negotiation; Japan is still not the equal of France, England, Russia, and America—this affair was originally a war without just cause, yet it nearly shook the whole situation; only after exhausting pen contention and tongue battle did it come within bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Japan's raid on Taiwan has only just been settled—and Japan is not yet in the class of France, Britain, Russia, or America. That unjust war nearly shook the entire realm; only after exhausting debate was it contained.

sentences.zh: 若泰西強大各國環而相伺，得中國一無理之端，藉為名義，構兵而來，更不知如何要挾，如何挽回？

translations.literal: If the powerful countries of the West encircle and watch one another, gain one unreasonable point from China, borrow it as a pretext, and raise armies to come—how much more would we know how to extort or how to recover?
translations.idiomatic: If the great Western powers, watching from every side, seized one unreasonable pretext to make war, who knows what demands they would impose or how we could recover?

sentences.zh: 言念及此，真有食不下嚥者，則自強之計尚可須臾緩哉？

translations.literal: Speaking and thinking to this point, there truly are those who cannot swallow food—then can the plan of self-strengthening still be delayed for a moment?
translations.idiomatic: The thought alone is enough to choke one's appetite. Can self-strengthening wait another moment?

sentences.zh: 此總理衙門奏請飭令會議諸條，實為緊要關係，不可不及早切實籌辦者也。

translations.literal: These items for which the Zongli Yamen memorialized and requested an edict ordering conference are truly of urgent relation and cannot fail to be planned and carried out early, concretely, and in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: The items the Zongli Yamen asks the court to deliberate are urgently important and must be planned and implemented without delay.

sentences.zh: 今計各疆吏遵旨籌議，指日將依限上陳，如飭下廷議，非向來會議事件可比，應由各王大臣期定數日，詳細籌商，將事之本末始終，一律貫澈，利害之輕重，條議之行止，辦法切實，折中定見，無蹈從前會議故習。

translations.literal: Now calculating that each frontier official, obeying the edict, is planning deliberation and within days will report within the deadline—if sent down for court deliberation, it is not comparable to conference affairs of former times; the princes and grand ministers should fix several days, deliberate in detail, carry through from beginning to end the root and branch of the matter, weigh light and heavy in benefit and harm, decide which items go forward or stop, make methods concrete, settle opinion by compromise, and not follow former conference habits.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier officials will soon report as ordered. If the matter is sent down for court deliberation, it is unlike ordinary conference business: the princes and senior ministers should set aside several days to deliberate in detail, carry the matter through from beginning to end, weigh the relative importance of benefit and harm, decide which proposals should proceed or stop, settle on practical methods and a balanced conclusion, and avoid falling into the old habits of previous conferences.

sentences.zh: 如今日議之行之，而異日不能同心堅持，則不如不辦。

translations.literal: If today we deliberate and carry out, yet another day cannot unite heart and hold firm, then better not to undertake at all.
translations.idiomatic: If we adopt plans today but cannot sustain them with united resolve tomorrow, we had better not begin at all.

sentences.zh: 如事雖議行，而名是實非，徒為開銷帑需，增益各省人員差使名目，亦不如不辦。

translations.literal: If affairs are deliberated and carried out in name but not in reality, merely opening expenditure of treasury needs and increasing nominal posts and missions for personnel in each province—better also not to undertake.
translations.idiomatic: If measures are adopted in name only, wasting treasury funds and multiplying empty posts across the provinces, it would be better not to act at all.

sentences.zh: 度勢揆時，料敵審己，實有萬萬不能不辦之勢，亦實有萬萬不可再誤之機。

translations.literal: Gauging the situation and measuring the times, estimating the enemy and examining oneself—there truly is a momentum of ten thousand times ten thousand in which action cannot be avoided, and truly a moment of ten thousand times ten thousand in which error cannot be repeated.
translations.idiomatic: Read the trends, judge the moment, weigh the enemy against ourselves: there is an overwhelming necessity to act, and an equally overwhelming need not to miss our chance again.

sentences.zh: 一誤即不能復更，不辦即不堪設想。

translations.literal: One error and it cannot be changed again; not to undertake and it cannot be borne to imagine.
translations.idiomatic: One mistake cannot be undone; failure to act is unthinkable.

sentences.zh: 總理衙門摺內所謂'必須上下一心，內外一心，局中局外一心，且歷久永遠一心'，即此意也。

translations.literal: What the Zongli Yamen memorial calls 'there must be one heart above and below, one heart within and without, one heart inside and outside the bureau, and enduring one heart forever'—is this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongli Yamen memorial's demand that "the court and provinces, the capital and the provinces, those inside and outside the Yamen, must all be of one mind—and remain so for the long term" expresses exactly this.

sentences.zh: 而大本所在，尤望我皇上切念而健行之。

translations.literal: Yet where the great root lies, I especially hope Our Emperor will earnestly keep it in mind and vigorously carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation lies here above all; I earnestly pray that Your Majesty will keep this close at heart and pursue it with vigor.

sentences.zh: 總理衙門承辦之事，能否維持，全視實力之能否深恃。

translations.literal: Whether affairs undertaken by the Zongli Yamen can be sustained depends entirely on whether real strength can be deeply relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the Yamen's work can be sustained depends entirely on whether we can build strength deep enough to rely on.

sentences.zh: 必確有可戰可守之實，庶可握不戰之勝。

translations.literal: One must have solid reality in which one can fight and hold, then one may grasp victory without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Only with real capacity to fight and to hold ground can we secure victory without war.

sentences.zh: 惟我皇上念茲在茲，則在事諸臣之苦心，自能上邀宸鑑。

translations.literal: Only if Our Emperor keeps this ever in mind will the painstaking effort of the ministers engaged in the affair naturally ascend to win imperial perception.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty keeps this always in mind, the devoted labor of those charged with these affairs will surely win the imperial eye.

sentences.zh: 凡百臣工亦人人有求知此事共籌此事之心，其才識智力必有百倍於臣者。

translations.literal: All officials too will each have the mind to seek knowledge of this matter and jointly plan this matter; their talent, insight, and intelligence will surely be a hundredfold beyond this minister's.
translations.idiomatic: Every official will then bring his mind to learning and planning together; many will surely surpass this humble servant a hundredfold in talent and judgment.

sentences.zh: 否則支持既難，變更不免，變而復合，痛心之端，必且百倍今日，非臣之所忍言矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise support will already be difficult, change cannot be avoided, change and again reunion—the beginnings of heartbreak will surely be a hundredfold today's, not what this minister can bear to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise support will fail, change will become inevitable, and after disruption and forced reversal the anguish will surely exceed today's a hundredfold—more than I can bring myself to say."

sentences.zh: 疏上，未幾卒。

translations.literal: The memorial went up; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted; before long he died.

sentences.zh: 溫詔賜卹，稱其「清正持躬，精詳謀國，忠純亮直，誠懇公明，為國家股肱心膂之臣」，贈太傅，予騎都尉世職，入祀賢良祠，賜銀三千兩治喪，遣貝勒載澂奠醊，諡文忠，歸葬盛京，命將軍崇實往賜祭。

translations.literal: A warm edict granted condolence gifts, praising him as "upright in personal conduct, meticulous in planning for the state, loyal and pure, bright and straight, sincere and earnest, fair and clear—a minister who is the state's sinews and heart," posthumously appointing him Grand Tutor, granting hereditary Captaincy of Cavalry, induction into the Shrine of Worthies, three thousand taels of silver for the funeral, dispatch of Prince Zaicheng to offer libations, posthumous title Wenzhong, burial in Mukden, and ordering General Chong Shi to go and confer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: A warm edict granted condolences, praising him as "upright in conduct, meticulous in statecraft, loyal and pure, bright and straightforward, sincere and fair—a pillar of the realm." He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted a hereditary Captain of Cavalry, inducted into the Shrine of Worthies, given three thousand taels for the funeral, and libations were offered by Prince Zaicheng. He received the posthumous title Wenzhong, was buried in Mukden, and General Chong Shi was sent to perform the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 十五年，皇太后歸政，追念前勞，賜祭一壇。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when the Empress Dowager returned power, recalling former service, she granted one altar of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when the Empress Dowager returned power, she recalled his earlier service and granted one altar of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 文祥忠勤，為中興樞臣之冠。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang was loyal and diligent, the foremost of the restoration Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang was loyal and diligent—the foremost Grand Councilor of the restoration era.

sentences.zh: 清操絕人，家如寒素。

translations.literal: His pure integrity surpassed others; his household was like that of the poor.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was unmatched; his household lived as plainly as a poor scholar's.

sentences.zh: 謀國深遠，當新疆軍事漸定，與俄國議交還伊犁，大學士左宗棠引以自任，文祥力主之，奏請專任。

translations.literal: His planning for the state was far-sighted; when Xinjiang military affairs gradually settled and Russia was negotiated with for the return of Ili, Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang took the task upon himself—Wen Xiang strongly upheld it and memorialized requesting sole appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He planned for the state with far sight. When Xinjiang was nearly pacified and Russia was to return Ili, Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang took the mission on himself; Wen Xiang strongly backed him and memorialized that Zuo be given sole charge.

sentences.zh: 文祥既歿，後乃遣侍郎崇厚赴俄國，為所迫脅，擅允條款，朝論譁然。

translations.literal: After Wen Xiang had died, later Vice Minister Chonghou was sent to Russia, was coerced by them, and on his own authority assented to the terms—the court was in an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Xiang's death, Vice Minister Chonghou was sent to Russia, was coerced into terms, and assented on his own authority—throwing the court into uproar.

sentences.zh: 譴罪崇厚，易以曾紀澤往，久之乃定議，倖免大釁。

translations.literal: Chonghou was condemned and punished; Zeng Jize was substituted to go; only after a long time was the agreement settled, fortunately avoiding a great breach.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghou was punished and replaced by Zeng Jize; only after long negotiation was a settlement reached, narrowly averting a major rupture.

sentences.zh: 法越事起，和戰屢更，以海防疏，不能大創敵，遷就結局。

translations.literal: The Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; peace and war changed repeatedly; because coastal defense was lax, the enemy could not be greatly struck, and a compromise settlement was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Franco-Vietnamese crisis erupted, policy swung between peace and war; coastal defenses proved too weak for a decisive blow, and the court settled for compromise.

sentences.zh: 及興海軍，未能竭全力以成之，卒挫於日本。

translations.literal: When the navy was raised, full strength could not be exhausted to complete it, and in the end it was defeated by Japan.
translations.idiomatic: When the navy was built up, the state could not commit its full strength; in the end it was shattered by Japan.

sentences.zh: 皆如文祥所慮，而朝局數變，日以多事矣。

translations.literal: All were as Wen Xiang had feared, while the court situation changed repeatedly and daily grew more troubled.
translations.idiomatic: All unfolded as Wen Xiang had feared, while the court shifted from crisis to crisis and daily grew more burdened.

sentences.zh: 子熙治，以員外郎襲騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: His son Xizhi inherited the hereditary Captaincy of Cavalry as an outer-court secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xizhi inherited the hereditary Captain of Cavalry while serving as an outer-court secretary.

sentences.zh: 寶鋆，字佩蘅，索綽絡氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，世居吉林。

translations.literal: Bao Yun, style name Peiheng, of the Suochuoluo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner whose family had long resided in Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yun, whose style was Peiheng, belonged to the Suochuoluo clan of the Manchu Bordered White Banner; his family had long lived in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，授禮部主事，擢中允。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a secretary in the Board of Rites, and was promoted to middle attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1838, was appointed a secretary in the Board of Rites, and was promoted to middle attendant.

sentences.zh: 三遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted through three transfers, reaching reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through three postings to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪竄兩湖，寶鋆疏請鄰近諸省力行堅壁清野之策。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Cantonese bandits raided the two Hu provinces; Bao Yun memorialized asking neighboring provinces vigorously to implement the policy of fortifying strongpoints and clearing the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852, when Cantonese rebels swept into Hunan and Hubei, Bao Yun memorialized urging neighboring provinces to enforce fortify-and-clear tactics.

sentences.zh: 四年，命往三音諾顏部賜奠，謝絕餽贐，外籓敬之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to go to the Sain Noyan Khan department to present condolences, declined all gifts, and the outer vassals respected him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he was sent to the Sain Noyan Khan league to offer condolences, refused all gifts, and won the respect of the frontier princes.

sentences.zh: 擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷禮部侍郎，兼正紅旗蒙古副都統，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Mongol Vice Commander of the Plain Red Banner, and was moved to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he became Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Mongol vice commander of the Plain Red Banner, and was transferred to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 八年，典浙江鄉試，以廣額加中官生一名，坐違制，鐫一級留任，文宗諭「寶鋆素以果敢自命，亦同瞻徇」，特嚴斥焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination; for expanding the quota and adding one official graduate he was found in violation of regulations, demoted one grade and retained in office; the Wenzong Emperor issued an edict, "Bao Yun has always styled himself bold and decisive, yet shares in favoritism," and specially sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination; for expanding the quota and adding an official graduate he was found in violation, demoted one grade but kept in office. Emperor Xianfeng issued an edict, "Bao Yun has always styled himself bold and decisive, yet shares in favoritism," and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 十年，命赴天津驗收海運漕糧，复赴通州察視，迭疏請定杜弊章程，並劾監督貽誤，如所請行。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to Tianjin to inspect and receive sea-transport tribute grain, again went to Tongzhou to inspect, repeatedly memorialized to fix rules against abuses, and impeached supervisors for delay—as requested, it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he was sent to Tianjin to inspect sea-transport tribute grain, then to Tongzhou to review the route. He repeatedly memorialized for rules against abuse and impeached negligent supervisors; the court adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 任總管內務府大臣，署理戶部三庫事務，會辦京城巡防。

translations.literal: He served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household Department, acting manager of the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue, and joint commissioner for capital patrol defense.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supervising minister of the Imperial Household, acting manager of the Board of Revenue's three treasuries, and joint commissioner for the capital's patrol defense.

sentences.zh: 時英法聯軍內犯，車駕幸熱河，既至，命提庫帑二十萬兩修葺行宮。

translations.literal: At the time the Anglo-French allied armies invaded inland; the imperial carriage went to Rehe, and on arrival an order was issued to draw two hundred thousand taels from the treasury to repair the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Anglo-French allies invaded, the court fled to Rehe and ordered two hundred thousand taels from the treasury to repair the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 寶鋆以國用方亟，持不可。

translations.literal: Bao Yun, because state finances were urgently strained, maintained it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yun argued that state finances were desperately strained and opposed the expenditure.

sentences.zh: 上怒，欲加嚴譴，會所管三山被掠，詔切責，降五品頂戴。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to add severe punishment; coincidentally the three mountains under his charge were plundered, and an edict sharply rebuked him and reduced him to a fifth-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and nearly punished him severely; when the three imperial parks under his charge were looted, an edict sharply rebuked him and reduced his rank button to the fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 踰月後，以巡防勞勚，復之，兼鑲紅旗護軍統領，复兼署正紅旗漢軍都統、左翼前鋒統領。

translations.literal: After more than a month, because of labor in patrol defense, he was restored, also made Guard Commander of the Bordered Red Banner, and again concurrently acting Commander of the Plain Red Banner Han Army and Left Vanguard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: After a month his rank was restored for his work on patrol defense; he was also made guard commander of the Bordered Red Banner and concurrently acting commander of the Plain Red Banner Han Army and the Left Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 十一年，文宗崩於行在。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Wenzong Emperor died at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 Emperor Xianfeng died at the Rehe traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 十月，穆宗回京，命在軍機大臣上行走，並充總理各國事務大臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Emperor Muzong returned to the capital; he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council and also appointed minister of the General Management of Affairs of All Foreign Countries.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Emperor Tongzhi returned to Beijing; Bao Yun was appointed to the Grand Council and made a minister of the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，奏劾壽莊公主府首領太監張玉蒼出言無狀，嚴旨逮訊，玉蒼治如律。

translations.literal: In the second year he memorialized impeaching Zhang Yucang, chief eunuch of Princess Shouzhuang's residence, for improper speech; a stern edict ordered arrest and interrogation, and Yucang was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he impeached Zhang Yucang, chief eunuch of Princess Shouzhuang's household, for insolent speech; the court ordered his arrest, and Zhang was punished by law.

sentences.zh: 三年，命大臣輪班進講治平寶鑑，寶鋆與焉。

translations.literal: In the third year ministers were ordered to lecture in rotation on the Records of Governance and Tranquility; Bao Yun was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 senior ministers were ordered to lecture in rotation on the Records of Governance and Tranquility; Bao Yun was among them.

sentences.zh: 江寧克復，以翊贊功，加太子少保，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When Nanjing was recovered, for assisting merit he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing was recovered, he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the peacock feather for his supporting role.

sentences.zh: 四年，命佩帶內務府印鑰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered to wear the seal key of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he was entrusted with the seal of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 尋以樞務事繁，請解內務府大臣職，允之。

translations.literal: Soon because Grand Council affairs were numerous, he asked to be relieved of the Imperial Household minister post; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing the press of Grand Council business, he asked to resign from the Imperial Household; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 自設立總理各國事務衙門，始求通知外國語言文字，置同文館，肄習西學，廷臣每以為非。

translations.literal: From the establishment of the Office for the General Management of Affairs of All Foreign Countries, they first sought knowledge of foreign languages and scripts, set up the Tongwen Guan, and studied Western learning—court ministers often thought it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zongli Yamen was founded, the court sought knowledge of foreign languages, established the Tongwen Guan, and began Western studies—measures many courtiers opposed.

sentences.zh: 六年，都察院代奏職員楊廷熙上書請撤同文館，語涉恭親王及寶鋆等專擅挾持，於是寶鋆偕恭親王請罷直候查辦，溫詔慰留，勉以不避嫌怨，勿因浮言推諉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Censorate substitute clerk Yang Tingxi submitted a memorial asking to abolish the Tongwen Guan; his words implicated Prince Gong and Bao Yun and others in monopolizing and manipulating power—thereupon Bao Yun together with Prince Gong asked to leave duty and await investigation; a warm edict comforted and retained them, urging them not to avoid suspicion and resentment and not to push off duties because of floating talk.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 Yang Tingxi, a substitute censorate clerk, memorialized to abolish the Tongwen Guan and accused Prince Gong, Bao Yun, and others of monopolizing power. Bao Yun and Prince Gong asked to resign pending investigation; a warm edict kept them in office and urged them not to shrink from criticism or defer to rumor.

sentences.zh: 七年，直東捻匪肅清，加軍功二級。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Nian bandits of Zhili and the east were pacified; he was given two grades of military merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868, when the Nian rebels of Zhili and Shandong were suppressed, he was granted two grades of military merit.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 he was transferred to the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 穆宗大婚禮成，加太子太保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong's grand wedding ceremony was completed, he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Tongzhi's wedding was completed, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兼翰林院掌院學士，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was concurrently Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and, as Minister of Civil Office, associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1873 he became concurrently chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and associate grand secretary while serving as Minister of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 尋調兵部，拜體仁閣大學士，管理吏部。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Board of War, appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion, and directed the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he moved to the Board of War, was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion, and continued to direct the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，晉武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was advanced to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 he was promoted to grand secretary of the Hall of Martial Eminence.

sentences.zh: 四年，回疆肅清，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Muslim frontier was pacified; he received preferential commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878, when the Muslim frontier was pacified, he received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 寶鋆自同治初年預樞務，偕文祥和衷翊贊，通達政體，知人讓善，恭親王資其襄助，至是朝列漸分門戶。

translations.literal: From the early years of Tongzhi Bao Yun took part in Grand Council affairs, harmoniously assisting together with Wen Xiang, understanding the polity, knowing men and yielding to the good; Prince Gong relied on his help—by now the court ranks gradually divided into factions.
translations.idiomatic: From early Tongzhi Bao Yun served on the Grand Council, working in harmony with Wen Xiang. He understood government, knew talent, and yielded to the capable; Prince Gong relied on his support. By now, however, the court was dividing into factions.

sentences.zh: 文祥既歿，議論益紛，編修何金壽因旱災劾樞臣不職，請加訓責，詔斥恭親王、寶鋆等目擊時艱，毫無補救，嚴議革職，加恩改留任。

translations.literal: After Wen Xiang had died, opinion grew more chaotic; Compiler He Jinshou, because of drought disaster, impeached the Grand Councilors for dereliction and asked added rebuke; an edict rebuked Prince Gong, Bao Yun, and others for witnessing hard times with no remedy, severely deliberated dismissal from office, and by grace changed to retention in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Xiang's death, court debate grew fiercer. Compiler He Jinshou, citing drought, impeached the Grand Council for dereliction. An edict rebuked Prince Gong, Bao Yun, and others for witnessing crisis without remedy, ordered their dismissal, then by grace allowed them to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 五年，以題穆宗神主，加太子太傅，復以實錄告成，推恩其子景灃晉秩郎中，侄景星賜舉人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for inscribing Emperor Muzong's spirit tablet, he was given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; again, when the Veritable Records were completed, grace extended to his son Jingfeng, promoted in rank to director, and his nephew Jingxing was granted licentiate status.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879, for inscribing Emperor Tongzhi's spirit tablet, he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; when the Veritable Records were completed, his son Jingfeng was promoted to director and his nephew Jingxing was granted licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 七年，庶子陳寶琛以星變陳言，專劾寶鋆，請仿漢災異策免三公故事，立予罷斥。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Sub-Reader Chen Baochen, on a stellar omen, memorialized and specially impeached Bao Yun, asking to imitate the Han precedent of dismissing the three dukes on calamitous omens and immediately dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 Sub-Reader Chen Baochen, citing a celestial omen, impeached Bao Yun alone and asked that he be dismissed at once, following the Han precedent of removing the three highest ministers after calamitous signs.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「寶鋆在軍機大臣上行走有年，尚無過失。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Bao Yun has served on the Grand Council for many years without fault.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Bao Yun has served on the Grand Council for many years without fault.

sentences.zh: 陳寶琛謂其畏難巧卸，瞻徇情面，亦不能確有所指。

translations.literal: Chen Baochen says he shrinks from difficulty and cleverly shifts burdens, looks to favor and personal ties, yet cannot point to anything definite.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baochen accuses him of shirking hard tasks and showing favoritism, yet cannot point to anything specific.

sentences.zh: 惟既有此奏，自平時與王大臣等議事未能和衷共濟，致啟人言。

translations.literal: Yet since there is this memorial, it must be that in ordinary times in deliberating with princes and grand ministers he failed to harmonize hearts and work together, giving rise to public talk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because this memorial was submitted, he must have failed in ordinary deliberations with the princes and senior ministers to work in harmony, inviting gossip.

sentences.zh: 該大學士受恩深重，精力尚健，自當恪矢公忠，勉圖報稱，務宜殫精竭慮，力戒因循積習，用副委任。」

translations.literal: This Grand Secretary has received deep grace; his vigor is still sound—he should strictly devote himself to public loyalty, strive to repay obligation, exhaust mind and effort, vigorously guard against routine accumulated habits, and fulfill the commission."
translations.idiomatic: This grand secretary has received deep favor and still has his strength; he should devote himself to public duty, repay the throne, work with full energy, break free of routine habits, and fulfill his charge."

sentences.zh: 十年三月，軍機大臣自恭親王以下同日斥罷，詔：「寶鋆入直最久，責備宜嚴，姑念年老，特錄前勞，全其末路，以原品休致。」

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year the Grand Councilors from Prince Gong downward were dismissed on the same day; an edict said: "Bao Yun has served in the palace longest; rebuke should be strict, but considering his age, specially recording former merit, preserving his final path, let him retire at his original rank."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1884 the Grand Councilors from Prince Gong down were dismissed on the same day. An edict said: "Bao Yun has served longest in the Council and deserves the sternest rebuke; yet considering his age, his past service is recorded and he is allowed to retire at his original rank."

sentences.zh: 十二年，皇太后懿旨加恩，改以大學士致仕，賞食半俸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Empress Dowager's gracious edict added favor, changing to retirement as Grand Secretary and granting half salary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886 the Empress Dowager graciously raised his status to retirement as grand secretary and granted half salary.

sentences.zh: 寶鋆退休後，時偕恭親王居西山遊覽唱和。

translations.literal: After Bao Yun retired, he often together with Prince Gong lived on the Western Hills, touring and exchanging verse.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement Bao Yun often joined Prince Gong on the Western Hills, sightseeing and exchanging poetry.

sentences.zh: 年逾八十，恩賚猶及。

translations.literal: Past eighty years of age, imperial gifts still reached him.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty, he still received imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1891 he died.

sentences.zh: 遺疏入，詔褒其「忠清亮直，練達老成」，贈太保，祀賢良祠，擢子景灃四品京堂，賜孫廕桓舉人，遣貝勒載瀅奠醊，飾終之典，視在位無所減，諡文靖。

translations.literal: His death memorial entered; an edict praised him as "loyal and pure, bright and straight, practiced and mature in age," posthumously appointed Grand Mentor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, promoted his son Jingfeng to Fourth Rank Capital Bureau, granted his grandson Yin Huan licentiate status, dispatched Prince Zaiying to offer libations—the rites of final honor, compared with being in office, were in no way reduced; posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: When his death memorial arrived, an edict praised him as "loyal and pure, bright and seasoned." He was posthumously made Grand Mentor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, his son Jingfeng was promoted to Fourth Rank Capital Bureau, and his grandson Yin Huan was granted licentiate status. Prince Zaiying offered libations; the funeral honors were no less than if he had still held office. He received the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子景灃，官至廣州將軍，卒，諡誠慎。

translations.literal: His son Jingfeng rose to General of Guangzhou, died, posthumous title Chengshen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingfeng rose to general of Guangzhou; after his death he received the posthumous title Chengshen.

sentences.zh: 孫廕桓，光緒二十四年進士，歷官國子監司業，改乾清門頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: His grandson Yin Huan, jinshi in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu, served as vice director of the Directorate of Education, and was changed to First Rank Attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yin Huan passed the jinshi in 1898, served as vice director of the Imperial Academy, and was later appointed first-rank attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 論曰：咸、同之間，內憂外患，岌岌不可終日。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Between Xianfeng and Tongzhi, inner worry and outer peril made each day precarious beyond endurance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Between the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, domestic turmoil and foreign threat made each day seem the dynasty's last.

sentences.zh: 文慶倡言重用漢臣，俾曾國籓、胡林翼等得展經猷，以建中興之業，其功甚偉。

translations.literal: Wen Qing advocated employing Han ministers, enabling Zeng Guofan, Hu Linyi, and others to unfold statecraft and establish the restoration enterprise—his merit was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qing urged employing Han officials, enabling Zeng Guofan, Hu Linyi, and others to carry out their strategies and build the restoration—an achievement of great weight.

sentences.zh: 文祥、寶鋆襄贊恭親王，和輯邦交，削平寇亂。

translations.literal: Wen Xiang and Bao Yun assisted Prince Gong, harmonized foreign relations, and cut down bandit turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang and Bao Yun assisted Prince Gong in smoothing foreign relations and suppressing rebellion.

sentences.zh: 文祥尤力任艱鉅，公而忘私，為中外所倚賴，而朝議未一，猶不能盡其規略；

translations.literal: Wen Xiang especially bore hard and heavy tasks with strength, was public-minded and forgot private interest, was relied upon at home and abroad—yet court opinion was not united, and he still could not fully carry out his plans;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang above all shouldered the hardest burdens, putting the public good before private interest, and was trusted at home and abroad—yet because court opinion was divided, he could not fully carry out his designs;

sentences.zh: 晚年密陳大計，於數十年馭外得失，洞如觀火，一代興亡之龜鑑也。

translations.literal: In his late years he secretly memorialized the great plan; on several decades of gains and losses in managing foreigners he saw as clearly as watching fire—a tortoise mirror of one generation's rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years he secretly laid out the great design; on decades of success and failure in dealing with foreign powers he saw as clearly as fire in daylight—a mirror of the dynasty's fate.

sentences.zh: 寶鋆明達同之，貞毅不及，遂無以鎮紛囂而持國是。

translations.literal: Bao Yun was equally clear and penetrating, but did not reach his firm integrity and resolution, and thus could not quell clamor and uphold the national course.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Yun was equally clear-sighted but lacked his moral firmness; he could not still the clamor or hold the national course steady.

sentences.zh: 如文祥者，洵社稷臣哉！

translations.literal: Such as Wen Xiang—truly a minister of the altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Wen Xiang were truly pillars of the state!
